description: Worked example for the scene planner: the approved reference video (references/posiblo-v1, composition PosibloFirstTest), expressed in the planner's schema. Speech and scene times come from src/Composition.tsx, src/Motion.tsx and src/captions-final.json. The 'why' notes are an editorial reading of the reference written for the planner, not statements by the video's author.

sentences.text: נניח שיש לכם עסק ואתם מקבלים פניות מלקוחות בוואטסאפ, באתר ובפייסבוק.
אתם מעתיקים פרטים ידנית, שוכחים לחזור לחלק מהלקוחות [unclear clause omitted from captions]
עכשיו, אפשר לבנות סוכן AI שיטפל בבעיה הזו כמובן, אבל אולי בכלל מספיק לחבר בין המערכות וליצור אוטומציה פשוטה שתעשה את העבודה.
המטרה היא לא להכניס בכל מחיר AI לעסק שלכם.
המטרה היא לחסוך לכם זמן לצמצם טעויות ולגרום לעסק לעבוד טוב יותר.
אז לפני שאתם משקיעים בטכנולוגיה חדשה, תשאלו את עצמכם, איזו בעיה בעצם אני מנסה לפתור?

decision: Four scenes in 43 s, each tied to one idea the viewer should see rather than only hear: the manual workflow problem, the simpler connected workflow, the three business goals, and the closing question. The opening line is the on-screen title, and the two punchy lines in the middle stay on the speaker, because their force is in the delivery, not in a diagram.

scenes.actualTiming: 4.8-14.3 s: starts as the channels are named and ends when the problem description ends.
scenes.heading: הפניות מגיעות. מה קורה אחר כך?
scenes.drawnAs: Three channel nodes converging into one manual-handling node, then two coral problem tags: 'פניות נשכחות', 'זמן על מעקב'.
scenes.why: The speaker describes a concrete process (leads arrive in three places, then are handled by hand) and its failure points. A diagram makes the bottleneck visible at a glance; listening alone does not.

scenes.actualTiming: 19.5-25 s: starts at 'אבל אולי בכלל מספיק', not at 'אפשר לבנות סוכן AI'; the scene shows the simpler option the speaker recommends, not the AI agent he sets aside.
scenes.heading: אולי מספיק לחבר בין המערכות.
scenes.drawnAs: A three-step connected workflow with animated connectors; the automation step is highlighted in lime.
scenes.why: The answer to the previous problem is again a process, so the same visual language shows the fix replacing the manual bottleneck. The scene illustrates the recommended path only.

scenes.actualTiming: 31.1-35.9 s: exactly the sentence that lists the three goals.
scenes.heading: טכנולוגיה עם תוצאה עסקית.
scenes.drawnAs: Three outcome cards revealed one by one, about 1.2 s apart (fixed delays, not word-timed).
scenes.why: A short list of three parallel outcomes, each a few words, is easier to remember as cards.

scenes.actualTiming: 38.2-42.7 s: starts at the question itself ('איזו בעיה...'), not at the start of the sentence, and holds to the end.
scenes.heading: איזו בעיה אני מנסה לפתור?
scenes.drawnAs: The question as large text, held to the end.
scenes.why: The video's takeaway. Showing the question gives the viewer one thing to keep.

noScene.why: The hook. It is the opening title on screen; a diagram would compete with the speaker's first line.
Short punchy lines ('וזה בדיוק העניין', 'המטרה היא לא להכניס בכל מחיר AI'). Their force is in the delivery, so the speaker stays full screen between scenes.

lessons: Scenes illustrate what the speaker explains or recommends, not every noun he mentions.
Between scenes the speaker returns to full screen; that rhythm keeps the person central.
Headings may frame the idea in a few words (for example as a question) but add no facts.
A scene starts on the words it illustrates, which can be inside a sentence.
